title: Red Violet Eyes M&A Growth as AI Identity Platform Expands Across Key Markets
excerpt: Red Violet (NASDAQ:RDVT) outlined its identity intelligence platform, growth strategy and plans to use recently raised capital for acquisitions during a comp...
content_html:
MarketBeat

Sat, August 29, 2026 at 7:01 AM EDT 6 min read

Key Points

  • Interested in Red Violet, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • Red Violet is expanding its AI-powered identity intelligence platform across collections, investigations, financial and corporate risk, emerging markets and real estate, serving more than 10,000 customers and an estimated $10 billion total addressable market.

  • The company is broadening its FOREWARN safety application beyond real estate into home healthcare, while continuing to grow its law-enforcement presence and other public-sector opportunities.

  • Red Violet raised approximately $115 million in equity to fund acquisitions, sales initiatives and organic growth. Management is targeting gross margins above 90% and adjusted EBITDA margins of 60% to 65% as revenue scales on its largely fixed-cost platform.

  • Are These 3 Under-the-Radar AI Stocks the Next Big Growth Stories?

Red Violet (NASDAQ:RDVT) outlined its identity intelligence platform, growth strategy and plans to use recently raised capital for acquisitions during a company presentation led by Camilo Ramirez, senior vice president of finance and head of investor relations.

Ramirez said the company seeks to provide identity-related information for transactions across the U.S. economy by aggregating disparate databases into what it describes as a 75-year longitudinal identity graph of the adult U.S. population. The platform is designed to help customers verify identities, assess fraud and financial-crime risk, conduct investigations and support safety-related screening.

→ Boeing's $131B F-15 Win: Mach 1 Momentum or Just Altitude?

He said Red Violet's management team has worked together for roughly three decades, including prior businesses that were sold to LexisNexis and TransUnion. Ramirez said the current company was designed as a cloud-native platform with artificial intelligence embedded from its inception, differentiating it from legacy systems built around data warehouses.

Five Vertical Markets

Red Violet serves five principal verticals: collections, investigative, financial and corporate risk, emerging markets, and real estate.

→ From SaaS-pocalypse to Perfect Storm: Workday's AI Growth Story Strengthens

In collections, Ramirez said customers use the company's data to locate the correct person, identify deceased consumers and flag bankruptcies before attempting collection activity. He described a "waterfall" model in which Red Violet may initially receive records that have already been unsuccessfully reviewed by other providers, then seeks to demonstrate a higher hit rate and move up in customer priority tiers.
